issues.legal_issue: Whether revenue records determine the designation of a village as an inam village.
material_facts: The lands were situated in villages treated as inam estates, and the court considered how the designation of an inam village is to be established.
The court held that the Government revenue accounts existing when the inam abolition legislation came into force are the primary evidence of the village’s designation.
issues.conclusion: A clear designation in the relevant revenue accounts is sufficient; if the entries are ambiguous and do not permit a definite conclusion, other relevant evidence admissible under the Evidence Act may be considered.
issues.legal_principle: In determining whether a village was designated as an inam village, the Government revenue accounts existing when the inam abolition legislation came into force are prima facie controlling. No further proof is required when they clearly show the designation; ambiguity permits consideration of other relevant admissible evidence.

predicates.inam_village_classification_proceeding: A proceeding requires a decision on whether a village was designated as an inam village.
predicates.revenue_entries_clear: The Government revenue accounts existing when the inam abolition legislation came into force clearly designate the village as an inam village or otherwise.
predicates.revenue_entries_ambiguous: The relevant Government revenue-account entries do not permit a definite conclusion about the village’s designation.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a village’s inam designation, its status is determined by clear revenue entries or, if those entries are ambiguous, by other admissible evidence.

issues.legal_issue: The meaning of private land in an inam estate requires land to have the character of domain or home-farm land retained for the landholder’s personal use and cultivation.
material_facts: The dispute concerned claims by landholders to ryotwari pattas for agricultural lands in inam estates.
The relevant statutory definition included the domain or home-farm land of a landholder.
The court considered the statutory scheme alongside the permanent occupancy rights conferred on tenants in ryoti land.
issues.conclusion: Domain or home-farm land means land appurtenant to the landholder’s residence and retained for personal use, cultivated by the landholder or under personal supervision; merely owning both interests in the land or letting it on short leases does not establish that character.
issues.legal_principle: The court harmonized sections 3(10)(b)(i) and 3(16) of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates Land Act, 1908, with sections 13 and 15 of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, and the tenant occupancy-right provisions. It applied Chidambaram Chettiar v. Santhanaramaswamy Odayar, [1968] 2 SCR 754, and P. Venkataswami v. D.S. Ramireddy, [1976] 3 SCC 665, and affirmed the approach in Zamindar of Chellapalli v. Rajalapati Somayya, Jagadeesam Pillai v. Kuppammal, and Parish Priest of Karayar Parish v. Thiagarajaswami Devasthanam. It held that the relevant propositions in Periannan v. Amman Kovil, AIR 1952 Mad. 323 (FB), were no longer good law to the extent they departed from this test.

predicates.inam_estate_patta_determination: A proceeding determines entitlement to a ryotwari patta for land in an inam estate.
predicates.land_is_appurtenant_to_landholder_reside: The land is appurtenant to the landholder’s residence.
predicates.land_is_retained_for_personal_use: The landholder retains the land for the landholder’s personal use.
predicates.land_is_personally_cultivated_or_supervi: The landholder cultivates the land personally or under the landholder’s personal supervision.

issues.definition: In a patta determination for an inam estate, land appurtenant to the landholder’s residence, retained for personal use and personally cultivated or supervised, qualifies as private domain or home-farm land.

issues.legal_issue: A landholder does not establish that tenant-held land is private land merely by showing occasional changes of tenants, short-term leases, or variations in rent.
material_facts: The original character of the disputed lands, whether ryoti or private, was not known.
The landholders bore the burden of establishing that the lands were private land, and the statutory presumption was that land was not private land until the contrary was proved.
The lands were in the tenants’ possession; the landholders’ evidence showed occasional changes of tenants, short-term leases, and changes in rents.
The landholders did not establish personal cultivation or a clear intention to retain the lands for personal use and cultivation.
issues.conclusion: The landholders failed to prove that the lands were private land and were not entitled to ryotwari pattas on that basis; the tenants’ appeals were allowed and the decision restoring the tenants’ position was reinstated.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 185 of the Estates Land Act, 1908, land is presumed not to be private land until the landholder proves otherwise. Sections 13 and 15 of the Estates Abolition Act, 1948, require the relevant claim to be determined under the statutory scheme. The court applied Chidambaram Chettiar v. Santhanaramaswamy Odayar, [1968] 2 SCR 754, and P. Venkataswami v. D.S. Ramireddy, [1976] 3 SCC 665; it rejected, to the relevant extent, the propositions in Periannan v. Amman Kovil, AIR 1952 Mad. 323 (FB), that would allow such circumstances alone to establish private-land status. The statutory occupancy-right scheme required the claimed exception for private land to be construed strictly against the landholder and liberally in favour of the tenant.

rule.if: ryotwari_patta_proceeding and landholder_claims_private_land and tenants_remain_in_possession and land_character_is_unknown and only_tenancy_changes_or_short_leases_or_rent_variations_are_shown and not proof_of_personal_cultivation_or_clear_personal_use_intent

predicates.ryotwari_patta_proceeding: A proceeding determines competing claims to a ryotwari patta after an estate has been abolished.
predicates.landholder_claims_private_land: The landholder claims that the land is private land and seeks a patta on that basis.
predicates.tenants_remain_in_possession: Tenants are in possession of the disputed land.
predicates.land_character_is_unknown: The land’s original character as private or ryoti land has not been established.
predicates.only_tenancy_changes_or_short_leases_or_: The landholder’s evidence consists only of changes of tenants, short-term leases, or variations in rent.
predicates.proof_of_personal_cultivation_or_clear_p: Evidence establishes the landholder’s personal cultivation or a clear intention to retain the land for personal use and cultivation.

issues.definition: When a landholder claiming a patta for tenant-held land of unknown original character shows only tenancy or rent changes or short leases, without proof of personal cultivation or clear personal-use intent, the claim to private-land status fails and the tenant is entitled to a patta.
